newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Tel Aviv bourse hopes trading to resume Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Tel Aviv bourse hopes trading to resume Wednesday.

text.p: The Tel Aviv Stock Exchange said on Wednesday that it hoped to open for the main trading session after a strike by Bezeq Israel Telecom workers wreaked havoc with communications on Tuesday.

The TASE opened for the morning call market session of trading known as Meretz as usual and officials said they hoped the main afternoon session in the 100 most liquid stocks known as the Mishtanim would resume on schedule.
"We are planning to go ahead as usual," said TASE spokeswoman Etti Tutnauer, referring to the Mishatanim.
Mishtanim trading was cancelled on Tuesday when brokerage houses and banks could not get through to the exchange. Bonds traded as well as options on the Maof blue chip index and the dollar.
The Meretz session determines the market trend and executes small orders while the bulk of trading takes place in the later Mishtanim session.
A week-long strike over government plans to privatise more of Bezeq has curtailed telephone repair and operator information services. By Tuesday, it became increasingly difficult to make phone calls.

A trades union official said on Tuesday that workers would obey a labour court order and return to their jobs on Wednesday morning but Bezeq director general Ami Harel told Israel Radio that "to the best of my knowledge" workers had not complied.
Telephone services remained disrupted by 11:00 a.m. (0800 GMT) on Wednesday.
